column1: # THE CAMPAIGN DAY, machine-readable. The spine of campaign/calendar.md.
# Append-only. One row per in-game day or span that got played. The CURRENT DAY
# is max(day) -- derived, never stored, so it cannot drift.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the day count was kept in the DM's head and drifted until
# the player caught it on Torsat's illness. `calendar.md` was then made
# authoritative -- but it is prose, so "what day is it" was still a reading
# rather than a query, and it is the single most frequently needed fact in the
# campaign. See dlwork/tooling_plan.md, the demand-side table.
# calendar.md remains the NARRATIVE record and is much richer than this. This
# file carries only what a tool needs: the number, where the party was, and one
# line to recognise the day by.
# Seeded 2026-09-11 from calendar.md. Days 1-76 are summarised in spans where
# calendar.md itself does; the day NUMBERS are the load-bearing part.

column4: summary
Expedition 1. Into the caves.
Slept in area 5. Emerged about 11 p.m.
Torsat's rash and fever. Salvage sold, 170 gp. Surety before Ottir. Halm's mule in restitution.
The patrol begins. Osk met on the road.
Torsat clear. Wend still refusing.
Torsat fully fit.
WEND COMES ROUND, before anyone spoke. Coll's standing instruction given.
Outbound. The cold camp thirty yards off the road, four people, a fortnight old.
Nan and her two children walk in. Two men off Ellery's.
The party's first mule.
Two carts bought, 50 gp each. Dragon scales sold, 110 gp.
Wend's open-handed-where-it-is-finite rule adopted: iron and salt at cost, price visible.
THE CLIP SOLD. 1,200 gp. Rosewood 350 besides.
The Ludbury spend, 1,038 gp. Fenn paid at his gate.
Ede wants a month to shut up her cottage.
THE ARTICLES BEGUN. Ancel on the road, 11 -> 81. Wend takes the factorship.
WEND AND ANCEL, 127. Four buyers named; a penny in the pound for three years. Six unlisted hands to Marrow's on a written right of return.
Marrow paid in the square. Gyll pays restitution to the eleven, aloud, Ottir witnessing.
Market day. ~178 gp of small goods moved.
HASK, DELLIE AND ISTA BECOME 1st-LEVEL CHARACTERS. Art. 7 agreed: 8 gp the tod, cap 500.
Check-ins. Halm's standing want, unmet: "what I'd want is a RUN."
Perrin, usher of the hall, met riding north. 92, then 98.
Market day. Ottir's hearing.
EXPEDITION 7 SETS OUT. Nine underground for the first time.
The skeletons behind the secret door into area 9.
Wend: only half the small goods have sold.
CUDDY'S ANSWER ON THE CRAG. Holy water refused. The dwarf in irons told. Licence counselled.
THE PETITION. Licence granted and backdated.
Ottir and Yrtone ride home. The party is now a known quantity in Sir Aymer's country.
Toller finds the same hole Wend found. THE LETTER TO WACE, and the receipt trick.
South with Halm's cart. Wat rides for Draycot.
Marchford at dusk. Pell the carrier met: "Ludbury. That's the whole mystery."
THE VIAL IS NAMED: REALGAR. Father Doule is 5th level and Marchford has no font. The small-goods line closes, 573 on 357.
Lyde's terms met. 31 gp paid at his door; 18 owing in three quarters.
WACE'S RECEIPT ARRIVES. Toller pays ~250. Over a thousand gold for the first time. Wend turns the narrow loom round.
Expedition 8 outfitting. Six ropes, eight person-weeks standard rations.
EXPEDITION 8. The barrel re-coopered behind a spiked door.
Areas 8 and 9 stripped. One troglodyte on the loaded walk out.
HOME. The barrel sold to Holt, 58 gp. Wend's week of writing done a day early.
THE STRUCTURE SIGNED, art. 13. Nan can grade wool. The wool operation formed.
THE DWARF TO DRAYCOT. Hask leaves with the wool party.
Cuddy frail. A MAN HAS BEEN SENT ABOUT THE ANIMATED DEAD. Dellie taught the words. Home that evening.
Ottir on the chapel roof. Wend has no amounts. THE CARRIAGE GAP: "at cost" was ~60 gp below cost.
EXPEDITION 9 SETS OUT. Eight walk north at first light -- Hask is on the wool road and Rowe went with Halm. Night at Coll's basecamp.

IN. *** NEW STANDING FORMATION FOR EXPEDITION 9: rank 1 YRTONE (shield, sling) / DAVE (shield, sword) / TORSAT (BOW); rank 2 FRYTHON (darts) / TRISTLE (bow) / ISTA (lantern, darts); rank 3 DELLIE (shield, sling) / BLARTHO (shield, sling). *** Thirteen squares to the alcove at (17,13).

EXPEDITION 9 ENDS. Out at midday, past the empty basecamp without stopping, on the north road by one. ~13 miles before dark, camped on the road; into Wethersby mid-morning. TWO TROGLODYTES at (24,37) cost TORSAT A WEEK -- first character in the campaign to serve the DMG p.82 week under RAW, the house rule having been retired the same day. 94 xp. No treasure. A door in a bay off the y=35 corridor still unopened

EXPEDITION 10 GOES IN, two days after expedition 9 came out. SEVEN -- Torsat invalid at the Inn to day 87, Hask still on the wool road. *** FORMATION: rank 1 YRTONE (sling, shield) / DAVE (sword, shield) -- TWO MEN IN A CORRIDOR THAT FITS THREE; rank 2 FRYTHON (darts) / ISTA (lantern, darts) / TRISTLE (BOW, not the spear); rank 3 BLARTHO (sling, shield) / DELLIE (sling, shield). *** They came back for one thing: the plain iron-banded door in the bay off the y=35 corridor, walked past twice on day 79 without anybody listening at it

EXPEDITION 10 OUT at 11h06m under, the party's second-longest. Half an hour down the unmade outcrop in the dark to Coll's empty camp, and slept there. ALL SEVEN WALKED OUT. Dellie serving DMG p.82 until about day 88 -- the SECOND character in three days after Torsat. Taken: 36 arrows, a bronze statuette, 29 cp. Mapped: the whole north-east quarter, proved to be ONE CLOSED CIRCUIT hanging off the y=35 corridor, with B1's own confusion maze screening the middle of it

HOME. Left Coll's camp at first light, half an hour to the road and twenty miles south. Arrived in the evening. DELLIE INVALID to ~day 88, TORSAT to 87 -- two of nine out of action at once, for the first time in the campaign. *** THE WOOL PARTY IS DUE TODAY *** -- Hask, Nan, Tam, Halm, Rowe -- and Osk got back to Wethersby on the 81st, so Wend has already had him

CORRECTION to the row above, appended not rewritten. THE TIMELINE IS: out of the dungeon at round 666 on the 81st, about five in the evening; half an hour down the outcrop to Coll's camp; SLEPT THERE the night of the 81st-82nd; left at FIRST LIGHT ON THE 82nd and walked the twenty miles, ARRIVING WETHERSBY THE EVENING OF THE 82nd -- one day, as rules/overland.md says a laden march makes, and as day 46-47 attests with an invalid in the party. THE 83rd IS THE DAY AFTER: the wool party's due date, with the morning free before they come in

*** THE PARTY SPLITS. *** SOUTH WITH THE CARAVAN (5): Yrtone, Tristle, Ista, Blartho, Hask -- three carts, Wend's list as freight and THE FORTY JARS as the party's own cargo, with TAM representing Wend and doing her buying. Ista teaches the camp cooking and the work is shared. EAST AND SOUTH BY HORSE (2): DAVE AND FRYTHON on the party's two LIGHT riding horses, 60 miles a day, ON ROADS THE WHOLE WAY -- Marchford, Ludbury, then three days east to WRAYE for the library, the unidentified ring (L029) and a correspondent for Toller. Torsat (to 87) and Dellie (to ~88) at the Inn

THE RIDERS EAST: Dave and Frython out of Ludbury at first light on the 87th, three days east to WRAYE on good road, carrying NEOT'S PEARL and the unidentified ring. THE CARAVAN reaches Marchford the same day -- Yrtone, Tristle, Ista, Blartho, Hask and TAM, with Wend's list and the forty jars for Trebb. The two halves are now four days apart and cannot send word; the rendezvous is WETHERSBY

THE RIDERS TURN FOR HOME. Wraye at first light on the 90th, 200 miles by road -- Wraye to Ludbury 75, Ludbury to Marchford 50, Marchford to Wethersby 75 -- about three and a third days on light horses. *** THE ROAD HOME RUNS THROUGH LUDBURY AND NEOT IS IN IT, AND THERE IS NOTHING TO TELL HIM YET *** because the ring stays unread until Wethersby. FRYTHON'S BOOK NOW: shocking grasp, read magic, sleep, IDENTIFY, ENLARGE/REDUCE -- 5 of a maximum 14 against a minimum of 8. CHARM PERSON CLOSED FOREVER at INT 17 (L049)

THE RIDERS PASS THROUGH MARCHFORD and do not stop for business -- Trebb had the forty jars off Yrtone on the 87th and there is nothing here for two men in a hurry. Out of Ludbury about midday on the 91st after Neot, ~30 miles before dark; a full 60 on the 92nd, which puts them 40 miles NORTH of Marchford by nightfall. *** THE CARAVAN IS ALREADY AHEAD OF THEM: *** Yrtone, Tristle, Ista, Blartho, Hask and Tam left Fenn's on the 88th, 100 miles by cart at 25 a day = four days, HOME ON THE 92nd. The two halves have been four days apart and unable to send word since the 84th and they miss each other on the road by one day

*** THE PARTY IS WHOLE AGAIN. *** Dave and Frython ride in mid-afternoon on the 93rd -- 125 miles Ludbury to Wethersby at 60 a day on LIGHT horses (rules/overland.md, DMG p.58), the caravan a day before them. NINE DAYS OUT, and the riders covered roughly 400 miles of it. WHAT THEY BRING BACK: enlarge/reduce and identify copied into Frython's book (5 spells of a max 14); charm person closed forever at INT 17 (L049); NEOT'S PEARL RETURNED UNSPENT because identify's window on the ring shut weeks ago; and ORDRIC, A SAGE AT WRAYE -- a name and a town and nothing else. THE RING IS STILL UNREAD. Torsat came off invalid on the 87th and Dellie about the 88th, so for the first time since day 83 ALL NINE ARE FIT

*** EXPEDITION 11 SETS OUT. NINE WALK NORTH -- the first time the whole party has gone underground together since day 45. *** Hask asked and free: Wend has the board to put up, four letters out to holders (L043), Bern waiting on a cloth decision and Fenn now hers entirely, but NONE OF IT IS HASK'S THIS WEEK (d6=1) -- he is her holder man, that work is done until the post comes back, and he would rather go down a hole than sit in town while letters travel. Out of Wethersby at first light, twenty miles to the crag turning, UNEVENTFUL ROAD (d6=5). Night at Coll's basecamp, empty as it always is -- which is the point of it. CARRIED: 11 person-weeks of food (8.5 standard + 2.5 iron = 77 person-days = 8.5 days for nine, and the iron half of that is an ESTIMATE the repo flags); 474 turns of light -- 15 sealed flasks, 1 broached, 8 torches, 52 turns in three lamps; 13 iron spikes with 9 still emplaced below; 7 sound ropes. NO OBJECTIVE DECLARED AND NONE ASKED FOR -- the party explores, and formation is given at the cave mouth, not in town

EXPEDITION 11 ENDS AT COLL'S BASECAMP. Out of the crag at round 854 on the evening of the 95th -- FOURTEEN HOURS FOURTEEN MINUTES, the longest ever by 54 minutes, and THE FIRST EXPEDITION OF ANY LENGTH WITH NO DAMAGE TAKEN BY ANYBODY. Half an hour down the unmade outcrop with 421 lb of salvage, made possible by ELEVEN carriers: BRAND and ORM came down with them. Night at the empty camp, Ista cooking for eleven, and nothing for Yrtone or Blartho to dress. Twenty miles south to Wethersby in the morning

*** THE SALVAGE DOES NOT COME. *** At first light in steady rain the party read its own encumbrance and stopped: 421 lb over eleven backs is 38 lb a head BEFORE mail and shield, which is the DMG p.58 HEAVY band -- ten miles a day, not twenty, so twenty-one miles to Wethersby becomes two days and a night in the open on 17.5 person-days of rations for eleven mouths. THEY STACKED IT ALL UNDER THE LEAN-TO INSTEAD and walked out light. Coll's trail is cart-passable to that flat and the carts are in Wethersby; they are coming back for it. Casters took the same loadouts they have carried all expedition. Out at first light, twenty-one miles down the north road in the wet, INTO WETHERSBY AT DUSK -- eleven of them, Brand and Orm included, and not one thing on the road all day.
MORNING: the buying, and MUND THE SMITH met for the first time in 96 days. AFTERNOON: north with two carts, three horses and twelve people.

*** NORTH WITH TWO CARTS, THREE HORSES AND TWELVE PEOPLE -- AND THEY ARRIVE IN THE DARK. *** The morning went on the buying: 51 gp of goods, MUND THE SMITH met for the first time in 96 days (reaction 52, neutral, he had 200 spikes and 20 lb of nails out of stock and said nothing about where his bar came from), and TWO FLASKS OF OIL because two is every flask in Wethersby. Eight person-weeks of rations was all the town could reach -- early spring, the hungry gap, 240 lb of food asked for in one morning off-market, two weeks at the PHB price and six at half over. *** THE COST OF SHOPPING FIRST IS DAYLIGHT: *** loaded and rolling by late morning, and a cart makes 25 miles in a day, so 21 miles ran out of light about two short of the crag turning. Up Coll's graded trail by lamp, into the empty basecamp somewhere near eight. NOTHING ON THE ROAD ALL DAY (d6=1) -- with 200 spikes, 20 lb of nails, 160 lb of food and three horses in the open, which is the load DESPERATE MEN came out for on the day-60 leg. Rain easing to grey and damp (d6=3). 454 lb of stores is 28 percent of ONE cart; the 421 lb of salvage still under the lean-to makes 82 percent of one between them, and there are two.
EXPEDITION 12. Eleven in, Rowe minding the camp. (23,22), then area 34's spikes, then the kitchen.

*** EXPEDITION 12: TWO HOURS AND ONE MINUTE, THE SHORTEST IN THE CAMPAIGN, AND THE SECOND CLEAN ONE RUNNING. *** In at dawn, out at round 121, nobody scratched, no monster seen, no door forced, no spike driven. A TOOL TRIP: they went in for one object and came out with three. CARRIED OUT: the large cast-iron kettle with 20 ft of riveted chain (180 lb) on a TWO-POLE SEDAN RIG the player designed -- a pole on each shoulder, front man and back man -- plus 13 pots and pans (10 sound, 3 holed and taken for scrap) and THE IRON SHEAVE BLOCK off the kitchen ceiling, which exists in the load only because the player asked why the hacksaws were supposedly in a cart. ~270 lb. FIVE WANDERING CHECKS INCLUDING THE FIRST clock.py extra IN CAMPAIGN HISTORY, bought by forty minutes of sawing iron -- ALL FIVE EMPTY. Then half an hour of unmade outcrop with 180 lb on poles: d6=4, slow and ugly with frequent rests and nothing broken and nobody hurt. Rowe had the camp and the animals the whole time. Day 99: twenty-one miles south to Wethersby with two carts and about 690 lb.

*** TIME-OF-DAY CORRECTION, player-caught: THE DM WROTE 'EVENING OF THE 98th' AND IT IS LATE MORNING. *** In at first light, 121 rounds under = TWO HOURS ONE MINUTE, then about an hour down the outcrop because of the kettle. That puts them back at the basecamp somewhere around TEN OR ELEVEN IN THE MORNING with the whole day in front of them, which is the entire reason the next thing is possible at all. The DM defaulted to 'evening' because every previous expedition has been eight to fourteen hours long and ended at dusk; a two-hour trip is a new shape and the habit wrote the wrong sentence. AND TORSAT IS 6/6 -- see hp_log, the first natural-healing row in the campaign. *** WHAT THE SPARE DAY BUYS: the party sets out to FIND THE DRY WATERCOURSE, the L053 rendezvous nobody has ever laid eyes on, three days before they must be standing in it with 37 gp. Rowe stays with the mules, the carts and 690 lb; the THREE HORSES go, LED not ridden, because a led horse is the cheapest possible test of whether a cart can follow.
